name: Healthy conifer canopy
hints: Reflectance drops sharply between Red and Green.
NIR reflectance is much higher than any visible band.
Sampled from intact, actively photosynthesizing canopy.
note: Live foliage absorbs visible light for photosynthesis but scatters NIR strongly at the leaf mesophyll.

name: Drought-stressed / senescent vegetation
hints: Red/NIR contrast is present but weaker than healthy canopy.
SWIR1 is elevated — canopy moisture is dropping.
note: As chlorophyll degrades and leaf water drops, visible reflectance rises and NIR falls.

name: Burn scar / char
hints: Every band is low — dark across the spectrum.
NIR collapses well below any vegetated curve.
SWIR only modestly elevated — residual ash/exposed soil.
note: Fire removes NIR-scattering leaf structure and deposits dark char, suppressing reflectance broadly.

name: Impervious surface (pavement/rooftop)
hints: Reflectance is moderate and fairly flat across all bands.
NIR is below any vegetated curve but clearly above water.
No chlorophyll feature, no gradual soil-like SWIR rise.
note: Pavement, rooftops, and concrete lack a chlorophyll or soil-mineral feature, so their curves sit at moderate, comparatively flat reflectance across all bands.

name: Bare soil
hints: Curve rises steadily from Blue through SWIR1.
SWIR1 is the single highest band.
note: Bare soil lacks a chlorophyll or leaf-structure feature, so its curve rises gradually with wavelength.

name: Open water
hints: Reflectance is low everywhere, near zero by NIR.
Blue/Green are the highest bands, not Red/NIR.
note: Water absorbs strongly with increasing wavelength — the near-inverse of a vegetation curve.
